text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn held talks with his Polish counterpart shortly after his arrival in Warsaw on Tuesday.

- Parliament yesterday passed a temporary measure granting the Health Insurance Fund HUF 6.5 bilion to keep hospitals and health institutions running. The House also passed a bill on credit institutes, financial enterprises and the State Monetary and Capital Market Supervision.
- The Foreign Ministry will cooperate with a parliamentary investigative commission to be formed in the near future to investigate the July summit meeting of ethnic Hungarians.

- Jacques Klein, head of the UN transitional administration in eastern Slavonia, conferred with Foreign Ministry State Secretary Istvan Szent-Ivanyi in Budapest yesterday on how Hungary could be involved in developing eastern Slavonia, which is due to revert to Croatian control shortly.
- The Budapest Stock Exchange Council suspended the trading rights of the securities firms Co-Nexus Ertekhaz Rt and First German Securities Ltd. in Hungary for an indefinite time on Monday.
- A Budapest court yesterday agreed with a motorist's claim that the HUF 1,000 fee on the M1 motorway is too high, and said it must be lowered to HUF 550.
NEPSZABADSAG

- The Federation of Hungarian Jewish Communities is severing ties with the Smallholders' Party, as in its view statements released by the party directed against Jews or that could stir up hostile sentiment against Jews are increasingly frequent.

- The ethnic Hungarian community in Romania should play a bridge-building role in relations between the two countries, according to Adrian Severin, the man tipped to be Romania's new foreign minister.

- The head of the Sub-Carpathian Hungarian Cultural Federation Miklos Kovacs addressed an open letter of President Arpad Goncz drawing attention to a 1994 resolution passed by the Sub-Carpathian People's Council declaring the Hungarian and German peoples as the eternal enemies of Ukrainians.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Croatian President Franjo Tudjman's official visit to Hungary scheduled for November 22-23 is being put off at the request of Croatia.
- President Arpad Goncz sent a letter of congratulations to Emil Constantinescu on his election as president of Romania.
- From November 22 the National Bank will no longer be in the foreign currency business.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- A six-party delegation flew to Brussels Tuesday to attend a two-day session of the EU-Hungary Associate Parliamentary Committee.

- The London office of Japanese investment bank Nomura has published its latest recommendations on Hungarian stocks, advocating TVK shares as a good buy and advising the holders of MOL shares to sell their papers.
VILAGGAZDASAG

- Domestic retail outlets and restaurants had combined sales of HUF 1,988 billion through the end of September, 19 percent more than last year calculated in current prices and 4 percent less in comparative prices.
- Pharmaceutical prices will go up by 18.5 percent on average next year.
- The porcelain producer Herendi Porcelan achieved sales of HUF 3 billion in the first ten months.
-- Budapest newsroom (36-1) 327 4040
